en: I praise that Lord of the Gaṇas, the son of Īśāna, who is delightful with the ringing sound of small bells, whose lotus-palms move in a fierce *tāṇḍava* dance, and upon whose shining, pot-bellied body rests a serpent as a necklace. || 1 ||

I praise that Lord of the Gaṇas, the son of Īśāna, whose face shines with the resonance of the lute of the destruction of sound, whose trunk-like staff gleams with a radiant bījapūra fruit, and who is encircled by swarms of bees hovering toward the fragrance of his trickling ichor. || 2 ||

I praise that Lord of the Gaṇas, the son of Īśāna, who is the singular light of dawn, red as the glow of the rising sun and the luster of coral and flowers; who has a protruding belly, a curved trunk, and a single tusk. || 3 ||

I praise that Lord of the Gaṇas, the son of Īśāna, who wears a crown adorned with a garland of various shimmering jewels and embellished by the crescent moon shining upon his diadem; he is the sole ground of all ornaments and the cause of the destruction of worldly existence.

I praise that Lord of the Gaṇas, the son of Īśāna, whose skill shines forth through the playful movement of his creeper-like brows— visible as the root of his vine-like arms are raised— and who is served by the chowries of the celestial nymphs.

I praise that Lord Gaṇeśa, the son of Īśāna, who is extolled by the best of yogis as the one whose pupils are tawny, throbbing, harsh, and restless; who is the incarnation of a noble and tender playfulness; and who resides within the digit of the moon.

I praise that bold and ancient one whom they call the single syllable, the stainless, the free from conceptual construction, beyond attributes, blissful, devoid of form, the supreme Oṃkāra, and the womb of the self of primordial wisdom.
Salutations to you, who are dense with the bliss of consciousness and peaceful; salutations to you, the creator and destroyer of the universe.
Salutations to you whose pastimes are infinite, the light of absolute liberation; salutations to the seed of the universe; be gracious, O Son of the Lord.

That mortal who, having risen early in the morning, recites this excellent hymn with devotion, shall obtain all desires through the grace of Gaṇeśa. When the Lord Gaṇeśa is pleased, his words are fulfilled; for what is difficult to attain when he is propitious?
